title: NBA Offseason Daily Digest
subtitle: September 4, 2026: Clippers Penalized, Thompson Extends, and Leonard's Future in Focus

items.headline: Clippers Hit with Landmark Penalties for Salary Cap Circumvention
items.summary: The NBA has levied severe penalties against the LA Clippers following a year-long investigation into salary cap circumvention involving Kawhi Leonard. The team was fined $30 million and will forfeit five first-round draft picks (2029-2033). Owner Steve Ballmer received a one-year suspension, as did President of Business Operations Gillian Zucker, while President of Basketball Operations Lawrence Frank was suspended for six months. Kawhi Leonard himself was fined $700,000.

items.headline: Rockets Lock Up Amen Thompson with Massive 5-Year, $208M Extension
items.summary: The Houston Rockets have secured their rising star Amen Thompson, signing him to a five-year, $208 million rookie-scale contract extension. The deal, which includes a 10% trade kicker, signals Houston's long-term commitment to the 23-year-old guard, who was the No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 NBA Draft.

items.headline: Jonathan Kuminga Signs with Minnesota Timberwolves
items.summary: Jonathan Kuminga has officially joined the Minnesota Timberwolves, agreeing to a two-year contract worth $13 million. The move comes after a summer of speculation, with Kuminga expected to step into the starting power forward role for the T-Wolves.

items.headline: Kawhi Leonard's Future: Toronto Raptors Trade Probability High
items.summary: Following the NBA's ruling on the Clippers' violations, the probability of Kawhi Leonard being traded to the Toronto Raptors has surged to 97% on prediction markets. A trade was reportedly agreed upon in principle in June, but was pending the outcome of the investigation.

items.headline: Pistons Face $200M Standoff with Jalen Duren
items.summary: The Detroit Pistons are reportedly at a standstill in contract negotiations with rising star Jalen Duren, facing a potential $200 million headache. Rival teams are said to be monitoring the situation closely.

items.headline: Fan Favorite Tacko Fall Returns to NBA with Philadelphia 76ers
items.summary: The 7-foot-6 fan favorite, Tacko Fall, is officially back in the NBA, signing with the Philadelphia 76ers. Fall, 30, spent recent years playing overseas and reunites with former Celtics teammate Jaylen Brown in Philadelphia.

items.headline: Stephen Curry Expresses Desire to Remain with Warriors Amid Extension Eligibility
items.summary: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry, under contract through the 2026-27 season for $62.6 million, is now eligible for a two-year extension worth up to $136.7 million. The 38-year-old has stated his clear intention to remain with the franchise for the rest of his career.

items.headline: Golden State Warriors Crowned 2026 NBA Summer League Champions
items.summary: The Golden State Warriors emerged victorious, defeating the Memphis Grizzlies in the championship game in Las Vegas to claim the 2026 NBA Summer League title.

items.headline: Yaxel Lendeborg Named Summer League MVP, Meleek Thomas Leads in Scoring
items.summary: Yaxel Lendeborg earned the title of 2026 Summer League MVP for his standout performances, while Meleek Thomas showcased his scoring prowess by leading the league with 28.3 points per game.
